chunks: And it is narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about a man who performed tamattu' and did not find what he could offer as a sacrificial animal, so he fasted three days. Then, when he completed his rites, it occurred to him to remain for a year.
He said: "Then let him consider the return point of the people of his town, and when he thinks that they have entered their town, then let him fast the seven days."

key_terms.مَنْهَلَ: the point or stage of return to one's home region
key_terms.ٱلسَّبْعَةَ ٱلْأَيَّامِ: the seven days of fasting required after return

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim performing tamattu' fast the seven days if he stays away and does not return home after completing the rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrificial animal and has already fasted the three days. If he remains away from his hometown for an extended period, he should estimate when the people of his town would have returned home, and then fast the remaining seven days. The narration clarifies how the timing of the seven-day fast is determined when actual return is delayed.
